title: Does AI learn from what you tell it?
style: warm cream light, teal accent, calm curious storytelling

lines: You open a chat with your *AI*.
You tell it your *name*, your *dog*, and your favorite *pizza*.

bg.intent: you open a chat and share a few personal details
subject: jake_neutral
chat

lines: It replies warmly, and it feels like you just made a *friend*.

bg.intent: a warm reply, a new friend
subject: jake_happy
chat

lines: The next day, you open a *new chat*.

bg.intent: a fresh, empty chat the next day
subject: jake_neutral
chat

lines: You ask, "What is my *dog's* name?"

bg.intent: you ask the AI about your dog
subject: jake_think
chat

lines: Your AI has *no idea*.
It does not know you at *all*.

bg.intent: the AI knows nothing about you
subject: jake_surprised
chat

lines: Ever wonder if AI *learns* from what you tell it?
And the strange part?
Your AI did *not forget*. There was *nothing* to forget.
But that does not mean your chats go *nowhere*.
Here is something *real*.
One AI company told personal users their chats may help *train* its models.

bg.intent: a real policy: chats may help train models
subject: jake_neutral
model

lines: Unless they switch a *setting* off.
ChatGPT has a similar switch, called *Improve the model for everyone*.
So which is it? Does AI learn from you, or *not*?
To find out, you need to know the *difference* between *training* and *chatting*.
*Training* is how the AI is *built*.
It reads huge amounts of text.

bg.intent: training builds the model from text
subject: jake_neutral
model

lines: It ends up as a fixed set of *numbers*.

bg.intent: the result is a fixed set of numbers
subject: jake_think
model

lines: Think of a printed *cookbook*.
Once it is printed, the recipes inside do not *change*.
But here is the *catch*.
*Chatting* is just using the finished cookbook.

bg.intent: re-hook: chatting only uses the finished model
subject: jake_happy
cookbook
chat

lines: When you chat, the AI *reads* and writes.
It does not *rewrite itself*.

bg.intent: the model reads but does not change
subject: jake_neutral
model

lines: So telling it your dog's name changes *nothing* inside the model.

bg.intent: your details do not change the model
subject: jake_blank
model

lines: Then how does it answer you *in the same chat*?

bg.intent: how does it keep track in one chat
subject: jake_confused
chat

lines: Every time you send a message, the app sends the *whole conversation* again.
Your first message, its reply, and your new question all travel in *one package*.
That package is its only *memory*.
Open a new chat, and the package is *empty*.

bg.intent: the package is the only memory
subject: jake_worried
package

lines: There is a limit too.
The AI can only read so much at once.
That limit is called the *context window*.
In a very long chat, older parts can get *lost*.
Some apps add a *memory* feature.
Saved *notes* are added to the package for each new chat.

bg.intent: memory is saved notes added to the package
subject: jake_happy
note
package

lines: Memory is its own *switch*, separate from training.
Real learning happens *later*, when a company builds a *new version*.

bg.intent: learning happens in a later model version
subject: jake_think
model

lines: So the answer is: *not while you chat*.
Your chat does not change the model *you are talking to*.
Your chats may still help train a *future version*, if that setting is *on*.

bg.intent: chats may still train a future version
subject: jake_neutral
toggle
model

lines: If you switch it off, that covers *future chats*, not training already *done*.
So first, open your *settings* and find the *data controls*.
Second, use a *temporary chat* for private things. ChatGPT leaves those out of training.

facts.claim: Training builds the model into a fixed set of numbers; chatting uses the finished model and does not change it
In a chat the model only sees the conversation so far, which the app sends again with each new message
A new chat starts fresh by default; nothing carries over unless an app adds it
A context window limits how much the model can read at once, and older parts of a very long chat can get lost
Memory is a separate feature from model training
Memory features work by adding saved notes to what the AI reads in new chats
Anthropic says personal Claude chats may be used to train future models unless the user switches the setting off
ChatGPT personal plans can use conversations to improve models by default; the Improve the model for everyone toggle turns it off
Turning the training setting off is forward-looking and does not remove data already used in past training
ChatGPT Temporary Chats are not used for training
Learning from chats happens when a company trains a new version, not inside the live chat

post.pinned_comment: The person in this story is fictional and the story is an illustration. Apps with a memory feature turned on can behave differently from the chat shown. The facts come from AI explainers and news reports: a trained model is fixed while you chat, each message is sent with the conversation so far, and some companies may use personal chats to help train future models unless you switch that off. Settings and policies change, so check your own app. The two tips are practical suggestions, not guarantees.
